intent.raw_query: Costa Rica eco-adventure, $2500, zip-lining and wildlife, February 2026 from Miami

experiences.name: Monteverde Cloud Forest Zip-Line Canopy Tour
experiences.description: Soar through the misty cloud forest canopy on one of Costa Rica's most thrilling zip-line circuits. With over 13 cables and Tarzan swings, you'll glide above the treetops spotting howler monkeys, toucans, and exotic orchids while experienced guides share insights about the unique cloud forest ecosystem.

experiences.name: Tortuguero National Park Wildlife Boat Safari
experiences.description: Glide through the jungle waterways of Tortuguero on a guided boat safari, spotting caimans, river otters, three-toed sloths, poison dart frogs, and over 300 bird species. If visiting between July and October, witness the awe-inspiring nesting of endangered green sea turtles on the beach at night.

experiences.name: Arenal Volcano Hanging Bridges & Rainforest Hike
experiences.description: Walk among the rainforest canopy on a network of 16 hanging bridges suspended high above the jungle floor near the iconic Arenal Volcano. This self-guided eco-walk offers incredible views of the volcano and exceptional wildlife spotting opportunities including toucans, morpho butterflies, and howler monkeys.

experiences.name: Manuel Antonio National Park Guided Wildlife Tour
experiences.description: Explore Costa Rica's most biodiverse national park with a certified naturalist guide who uses a high-powered spotting scope to reveal camouflaged wildlife invisible to the untrained eye. Encounter all four monkey species, two-toed sloths, Jesus Christ lizards, and stunning Pacific coastal beaches within the same park.

experiences.name: Corcovado National Park Jungle Expedition & Night Walk
experiences.description: Venture deep into one of the world's most biologically intense rainforests on the Osa Peninsula. A full-day guided trek through Corcovado reveals tapirs, scarlet macaws, white-lipped peccaries, and jaguars in their natural habitat. Cap the adventure with a guided night walk to spot tarantulas, tree frogs, and nocturnal mammals.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Costa Rica
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Juan Santamaría International Airport at 22:30 on flight UA. Clear customs and immigration, collect luggage, and arrange pre-booked budget shuttle or shared transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and rest.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the airport
meals.dinner: Grab a quick bite at the airport — Subway or a local soda (small Costa Rican diner) near the terminal. Budget ~$5–8 USD

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book a shared shuttle in advance (companies like Interbus or Caribe Shuttle cost $15–25 USD vs $50+ for a taxi). Have small USD or colones ready for tips. Keep essentials in carry-on for easy access upon late arrival.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. After a leisurely wake-up, explore the beachfront area on foot. Walk along the shoreline, get oriented with the local neighborhood, and find a nearby supermarket (Super Mas or Palí chain) to stock up on snacks, water, and breakfast staples to save money throughout the trip.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the nearest local beach for a relaxed afternoon. Swim, sunbathe, and watch for coastal wildlife such as pelicans, frigatebirds, and hermit crabs. Ask hotel staff about free or low-cost nearby nature trails. Many beachfront areas in Costa Rica have short mangrove or jungle paths accessible for free.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll into the nearest town center. Browse the local sodas (traditional Costa Rican diners) for an authentic and affordable dinner. Enjoy the laid-back beach town atmosphere and plan the week ahead.

meals.breakfast: Grab fruit, bread, and coffee from the local supermarket or a nearby soda — budget ~$3–5 USD
meals.lunch: Casado (rice, beans, salad, protein) at a local soda near the beach — budget ~$6–8 USD
meals.dinner: Fresh fish tacos or arroz con pollo at a local soda in town — budget ~$7–10 USD

day_by_day.notes: Day 2 is intentionally relaxed to allow jet lag recovery. Use this day to exchange currency if needed — look for a Banco Nacional or BCR ATM for the best rates. Avoid airport exchange counters.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early for a guided wildlife walk in a nearby nature reserve or national park. Manuel Antonio, Carara, or a local private reserve (depending on resort location) offer morning guided tours where wildlife is most active. Look for sloths, howler monkeys, toucans, and scarlet macaws. Budget guided tours start around $25–35 USD per person.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the wildlife walk, head to a nearby waterfall or swimming hole for a refreshing afternoon dip. Many waterfalls near Costa Rican beach towns are accessible via short hikes with little to no entrance fee. Ask locals or hotel staff for the closest hidden gem.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area. Cook a simple meal using supermarket groceries or enjoy a budget dinner at a local soda. Sit outside and listen for nocturnal wildlife — frogs, insects, and night birds are commonly heard near beachfront resorts.

meals.breakfast: Gallo pinto (rice and beans with egg) at a local soda or from supermarket supplies — budget ~$3–5 USD
meals.lunch: Pack a lunch from supermarket supplies (sandwiches, fruit, granola bars) to eat at the waterfall — budget ~$3–4 USD
meals.dinner: Casado with fresh catch of the day at a local soda — budget ~$8–10 USD

day_by_day.notes: Book the wildlife walk the evening before through the hotel or a local tour operator to secure a spot. Morning tours (starting 6:00–7:00 AM) offer the best wildlife sightings. Bring insect repellent, sunscreen, and a reusable water bottle.

day_by_day.morning: Zip-lining adventure! Book a budget zip-line tour through a local operator near the resort area. Many coastal and jungle areas of Costa Rica have zip-line canopy tours ranging from $45–65 USD per person for multi-line experiences. Enjoy the rush of soaring above the rainforest canopy while spotting monkeys and birds below.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the adrenaline of zip-lining, visit a nearby butterfly garden or frog sanctuary. These small eco-attractions typically cost $10–15 USD and offer incredible close-up wildlife encounters including poison dart frogs, morpho butterflies, and tropical reptiles.
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate the adventurous day with a sunset beach walk. Watch the famous Costa Rican sunset over the Pacific (if on the west coast) and enjoy a cold Imperial beer or fresh coconut water from a beach vendor (~$1–2 USD).

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast before the tour — gallo pinto and fresh fruit at a local soda — budget ~$4–6 USD
meals.lunch: Empanadas or bocas (small snacks) from a street vendor near the zip-line area — budget ~$4–6 USD
meals.dinner: Pizza or pasta at a slightly more casual tourist-friendly restaurant for a treat — budget ~$10–12 USD

day_by_day.notes: Book zip-lining at least 1–2 days in advance. Compare prices between operators — some offer combo packages (zip-line + wildlife walk) for better value. Wear closed-toe shoes and comfortable athletic clothing. Weight and health restrictions may apply.

day_by_day.morning: Take a budget day trip to a nearby national park (such as Manuel Antonio, Carara, or Tortuguero depending on resort location). Arrive early to beat the crowds and heat. Entrance fees are typically $18–20 USD for foreigners. Self-guided walks are free once inside — pick up a trail map at the entrance.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the national park. Spend time at a park beach (if available) for swimming and wildlife spotting. White-faced capuchin monkeys are famously bold in Manuel Antonio and may approach visitors. Keep food secured in your bag.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort by shared shuttle or local bus (buses cost $1–3 USD and are the most budget-friendly option). Rest and recharge with a home-cooked meal from supermarket supplies at the resort.

meals.breakfast: Pack a supermarket breakfast to eat on the bus or before entering the park — budget ~$3 USD
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch packed from supermarket supplies eaten at a park bench or beach — budget ~$4–5 USD
meals.dinner: Cook pasta or rice and beans in the resort kitchen (if available) or visit a local soda — budget ~$5–8 USD

day_by_day.notes: National parks in Costa Rica require advance online reservations (Sistema Nacional de Áreas de Conservación — SINAC website). Slots fill up fast, especially on weekends. Reserve 2–3 days ahead. Bring cash for entrance fees as card readers may be unreliable.

day_by_day.morning: Surfing or stand-up paddleboarding lesson on the beach. Many budget surf schools along Costa Rica's coasts offer 2-hour beginner lessons for $30–45 USD including board rental. Even non-surfers can enjoy a paddleboard rental for $15–20 USD per hour for a calm morning on the water.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore a nearby fishing village or small town by local bus or bicycle rental. Interact with locals, visit a farmers market if available, and browse artisan crafts. Look for handmade souvenirs like painted gourds, wood carvings, or coffee products at fair prices.
day_by_day.evening: Join a free or low-cost community event if available (check with hotel staff). Otherwise, enjoy a relaxed beachside dinner and stargaze on the beach — Costa Rica's rural areas have minimal light pollution and incredible night skies.

meals.breakfast: Fresh tropical fruit smoothie and toast at a beachside café — budget ~$4–6 USD
meals.lunch: Ceviche and patacones (fried plantains) from a beachside kiosk — budget ~$6–8 USD
meals.dinner: Grilled whole fish (pescado entero) at a local soda by the water — budget ~$9–12 USD

day_by_day.notes: Bicycle rentals typically cost $10–15 USD per day and are a great budget-friendly way to explore the local area. Always negotiate rental prices politely. Apply reef-safe sunscreen before water activities to protect Costa Rica's marine ecosystems.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and resort day. Sleep in, enjoy the beachfront, and take care of any laundry or admin tasks (many hostels and budget resorts offer coin laundry for $2–4 USD). Spend time journaling, reading, or simply relaxing in a hammock.
day_by_day.afternoon: Snorkeling excursion to a nearby reef or rocky point. Rent snorkel gear from a local shop ($10–15 USD) and explore independently, or join a budget group snorkeling tour ($25–35 USD) to access better reef sites with a guide who can identify marine life.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset happy hour at a beachfront bar. Many establishments offer 2-for-1 drink specials from 4:00–6:00 PM. Enjoy a local craft beer or fresh fruit cocktail while watching the sunset. Budget $5–8 USD for drinks.

meals.breakfast: Lazy brunch at the resort or a nearby café — gallo pinto, eggs, and fresh juice — budget ~$5–7 USD
meals.lunch: Sandwich and fruit from supermarket supplies eaten at the beach — budget ~$3–4 USD
meals.dinner: Shrimp stir-fry or seafood pasta at a mid-range local restaurant as a weekly treat — budget ~$12–15 USD

day_by_day.notes: Mid-trip rest day is important for sustainable travel energy. Use this day to review the remaining itinerary, confirm any upcoming bookings, and check in with home. Hydrate well — the tropical heat and activity level can be draining.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning birdwatching walk. Costa Rica is one of the world's top birdwatching destinations with over 900 species. Join a budget guided birdwatching tour ($20–30 USD) or do a self-guided walk at dawn with a free eBird app and binoculars (rentable from some tour operators for $5 USD). Look for toucans, resplendent quetzals (in highland areas), and scarlet macaws.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local cacao or coffee farm for an educational and delicious eco-tour. Many small family-run farms offer 1–2 hour tours for $15–25 USD that include tastings of fresh cacao, chocolate-making demonstrations, and insight into Costa Rica's agricultural heritage.
day_by_day.evening: Cook dinner at the resort using local ingredients purchased from a farmers market or supermarket. Try making a traditional Costa Rican meal: rice, black beans, fried plantains, and a simple chicken or vegetable stir-fry.

meals.breakfast: Pre-dawn coffee and a banana before the birdwatching walk — budget ~$2 USD
meals.lunch: Included tasting snacks at the cacao/coffee farm tour, supplemented by a light soda meal — budget ~$5–7 USD
meals.dinner: Home-cooked Costa Rican meal from supermarket ingredients — budget ~$5–7 USD for two meals worth of groceries

day_by_day.notes: Birdwatching is best from 5:30–8:00 AM when birds are most active and temperatures are cooler. Bring a light rain jacket as morning mist is common in forested areas. The cacao farm tour is an excellent sustainable tourism option that directly supports local families.

day_by_day.morning: White-water rafting day trip (if accessible from resort location — rivers like the Savegre or Naranjo are popular). Budget rafting tours on Class II–III rapids for beginners cost $55–75 USD including transport, guide, equipment, and lunch. This is one of Costa Rica's most thrilling eco-adventure experiences.
day_by_day.afternoon: Post-rafting, many tours include a stop at a natural hot spring or riverside swimming hole. Soak tired muscles and enjoy the jungle surroundings. If the tour doesn't include this, ask the guide to recommend a free nearby spot.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort exhausted and exhilarated. Light dinner and early bedtime to recover from the physical day.

meals.breakfast: Hearty breakfast before the physical activity — eggs, gallo pinto, and fruit at a local soda — budget ~$5–7 USD
meals.lunch: Typically included in the rafting tour package (riverside BBQ or packed lunch)
meals.dinner: Simple soup (sopa negra or chicken soup) and bread at a local soda — budget ~$6–8 USD

day_by_day.notes: White-water rafting availability depends on the resort's proximity to suitable rivers. Confirm with local tour operators 2–3 days in advance. Minimum age and swimming ability requirements apply. Waterproof your valuables and leave non-essentials at the resort. GoPro rentals may be available from the tour operator for ~$15 USD.

day_by_day.morning: Visit a wildlife rescue center or animal sanctuary. Costa Rica has several reputable rescue centers (like Kids Saving the Rainforest, Toucan Rescue Ranch, or local equivalents) that care for injured and orphaned wildlife. Entrance fees ($15–25 USD) directly fund animal care. See sloths, toucans, monkeys, and more up close.
day_by_day.afternoon: Kayaking or canoeing in a nearby estuary, mangrove forest, or calm bay. Mangrove kayaking tours ($30–45 USD) offer incredible wildlife encounters including crocodiles, herons, kingfishers, and monkeys in a peaceful setting. Many operators offer self-guided rentals for less.
day_by_day.evening: Night tour! Join a guided night walk in a nearby forest or garden ($20–30 USD) to spot nocturnal wildlife: red-eyed tree frogs, tarantulas, sleeping birds, bats, and luminescent insects. An unforgettable Costa Rican experience.

meals.breakfast: Yogurt, granola, and tropical fruit from supermarket supplies — budget ~$3–4 USD
meals.lunch: Wrap or sandwich packed from supermarket eaten during the kayaking break — budget ~$3–5 USD
meals.dinner: Quick soda dinner before the night tour — casado or arroz con pollo — budget ~$7–9 USD

day_by_day.notes: Book the night tour in advance as group sizes are limited. Wear long sleeves and pants for the night walk to protect against insects. The wildlife rescue center visit is one of the most ethically sound wildlife experiences available — avoid any attractions that allow selfies with wild animals or unnatural animal interactions.

day_by_day.morning: Horseback riding through jungle trails or along the beach. Many ranches near Costa Rican beach towns offer 2–3 hour guided horseback rides for $40–60 USD per person. This is a classic eco-adventure activity that allows access to terrain unreachable on foot and offers unique wildlife spotting opportunities.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local waterfall for swimming and relaxation. Many of Costa Rica's most beautiful waterfalls require only a short hike and have free or low-cost access. Bring a towel, water, and snacks for a perfect afternoon in nature.
day_by_day.evening: Souvenir shopping in the local town center. Look for ethically sourced and locally made products: handmade jewelry, painted tiles, organic coffee, and chocolate. Bargaining is acceptable at craft markets. Set a strict souvenir budget to stay on track financially.

meals.breakfast: Pinto and eggs at a local soda before the horseback ride — budget ~$4–6 USD
meals.lunch: Picnic at the waterfall — supermarket supplies including fruit, crackers, cheese, and juice — budget ~$4–5 USD
meals.dinner: Treat yourself to a slightly nicer dinner at a local restaurant with ocean views — grilled fish or shrimp — budget ~$13–16 USD

day_by_day.notes: Confirm horseback riding availability and weight limits with the operator in advance. Wear closed-toe shoes and long pants for riding. At the waterfall, be cautious of slippery rocks and strong currents. Never jump into unfamiliar water without checking depth first.

day_by_day.morning: Final full adventure day — combine a morning hike in the best local nature area you haven't yet visited. Use the knowledge gained throughout the trip to navigate independently, saving on guide fees. Bring all your gear: binoculars, camera, insect repellent, and plenty of water.
day_by_day.afternoon: Beach time and reflection. Spend the afternoon at your favorite beach spot from the trip. Swim, journal, and soak in the final full day in Costa Rica. Consider writing down top memories, wildlife spotted, and lessons learned for future travel.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at the best local soda or restaurant discovered during the trip. Splurge slightly within budget for a memorable final meal. Try a traditional dessert like tres leches cake or arroz con leche.

meals.breakfast: Full Costa Rican breakfast — gallo pinto, eggs, toast, fresh juice, and coffee at a local soda — budget ~$5–7 USD
meals.lunch: Ceviche and fresh coconut water at a beachside kiosk — budget ~$7–9 USD
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner — fresh lobster or whole snapper with sides at a well-loved local restaurant — budget ~$15–20 USD as a final splurge

day_by_day.notes: Use the afternoon to begin packing non-essentials and organize receipts and expenses. Donate any leftover non-perishable food to hotel staff or a local family. Leave a positive review for any local tour operators, sodas, or guides who made the trip special — it directly supports small Costa Rican businesses.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Costa Rica. Wake up early for one last sunrise beach walk or a quiet sit in the resort garden to listen to the birds and howler monkeys. Pack all remaining belongings, double-check the room for forgotten items, and check out of Aegean Bliss Resort.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrange shared shuttle or budget transfer to Juan Santamaría International Airport. Arrive at the airport at least 3 hours before international departure. Browse duty-free for last-minute coffee or chocolate gifts (Britt Coffee is a popular Costa Rican brand available in the airport). Clear security and immigration.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Costa Rica with incredible memories, wildlife photos, and a deeper appreciation for eco-adventure travel. Pura Vida!

meals.breakfast: Final gallo pinto breakfast at the resort or a nearby soda — budget ~$4–6 USD
meals.lunch: Airport meal — allow $10–15 USD for airport pricing
meals.dinner: On the plane or at connecting airport

day_by_day.notes: Confirm departure flight details the night before. Keep all important documents (passport, boarding pass, travel insurance) in an easily accessible bag. Exchange any remaining colones back to USD at the airport (rates are less favorable but convenient). Budget tip: save $28 USD cash for the Costa Rica airport departure tax if not already included in your ticket (most modern tickets include it — check your booking confirmation).

trip_options.title: Classic Costa Rica Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Juan Santamaría International Airport at 22:30. Clear customs and immigration, collect luggage, and arrange pre-booked private transfer or shared shuttle to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and get a good night's rest to prepare for the adventure ahead.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport before departure
meals.lunch: On the plane or at airport layover
meals.dinner: Grab a light snack at the airport arrival hall or a 24-hour soda (local diner) near the airport such as Soda Tapia — rice, beans, and a protein for ~$8–12

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange airport transfer before arrival to avoid stress late at night. Keep a small amount of Costa Rican colones or USD on hand for tips and snacks. The resort is beachfront so confirm exact directions with your hotel in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. After a leisurely wake-up, enjoy the resort's beachfront setting with a morning walk along the beach to get your bearings. Explore the immediate resort area and ask the concierge about the week's activity schedule.
day_by_day.afternoon: Orientation afternoon: Visit a nearby local market or town center to pick up essentials, exchange currency if needed, and sample local fruits like maracuyá, guanábana, and pipas (fresh coconuts). Take a relaxed swim or snorkel session in the ocean near the resort.
day_by_day.evening: Welcome dinner at the resort's restaurant or a nearby mid-range beachfront restaurant. Enjoy a classic Costa Rican casado (rice, black beans, plantains, salad, and choice of protein). Watch the sunset from the beach with a local Imperial beer or fresh agua de pipa.

meals.breakfast: Resort buffet breakfast — eggs, gallo pinto, fresh tropical fruit, coffee (~$10–15 if not included)
meals.lunch: Light snack at a local soda near the resort — ceviche and patacones for ~$8–10
meals.dinner: Beachfront mid-range restaurant near the resort — casado with fresh fish, plantains, and salad for ~$15–20

day_by_day.notes: This is a recovery and orientation day. Don't over-schedule — jet lag and travel fatigue are real. Confirm all upcoming activity bookings with the concierge today.

day_by_day.morning: Manuel Antonio National Park Guided Wildlife Tour: Head out early (7:00 AM) to beat the crowds at one of Costa Rica's most biodiverse national parks. A certified naturalist guide uses a high-powered spotting scope to help you find sloths, white-faced capuchin monkeys, squirrel monkeys, toucans, and poison dart frogs hidden in the lush jungle.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Manuel Antonio's pristine white-sand beaches within the park. Swim at Playa Manuel Antonio, one of the most beautiful beaches in Central America, surrounded by jungle. Spot more wildlife along the park's coastal trail.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort by late afternoon. Freshen up and head to a local restaurant in the Manuel Antonio village strip for dinner. Enjoy the vibrant atmosphere of this popular eco-tourism hub.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before 6:30 AM departure — gallo pinto, eggs, and coffee
meals.lunch: Pack a light lunch or purchase snacks inside the park — fruit, granola bars, and water (no food vendors inside the park)
meals.dinner: Restaurant La Cantina or similar mid-range spot in Manuel Antonio village — grilled mahi-mahi with rice and beans for ~$18–22

day_by_day.notes: Manuel Antonio National Park has a daily visitor cap — book tickets and the guided tour in advance online. Bring reef-safe sunscreen, insect repellent, water shoes, and a dry bag for beach time. The park is closed on Tuesdays.

day_by_day.morning: Depart early for Arenal Volcano area — approximately 3.5 to 4.5 hour drive through scenic mountain roads. Arrange a private driver or shared shuttle through the resort. Enjoy the changing landscape as you travel from the Pacific coast into the volcanic highlands.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check into a mid-range lodge near Arenal (such as Arenal Paraíso Resort or similar). After settling in, visit the Arenal Volcano hanging bridges for a self-guided walk — stroll across suspended bridges above the rainforest canopy with stunning volcano views.
day_by_day.evening: Soak in a natural hot spring fed by the Arenal Volcano's geothermal heat. Mid-range options like Baldi Hot Springs or Eco Termales offer beautiful pools and a relaxed atmosphere. Enjoy dinner at the hot springs' restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast before departure — gallo pinto and fresh fruit
meals.lunch: Stop at a roadside soda en route to Arenal — typical casado for ~$8–10
meals.dinner: Dinner at Baldi Hot Springs restaurant or a local Arenal town restaurant such as Restaurante Nene's — traditional Costa Rican cuisine for ~$15–20

day_by_day.notes: The drive from the Pacific coast to Arenal is scenic but long — start by 7:00–8:00 AM. Roads can be winding and occasionally unpaved; a 4WD vehicle is recommended. Book hot springs in advance as they fill up quickly in peak season.

day_by_day.morning: Arenal Volcano Hanging Bridges & Rainforest Hike (Full Experience): Join a guided tour through the network of 16 hanging bridges suspended high above the jungle floor in the Arenal Rainforest. Your naturalist guide will point out toucans, morpho butterflies, howler monkeys, and exotic orchids while explaining the complex layers of the rainforest ecosystem.
day_by_day.afternoon: Afternoon kayaking or stand-up paddleboarding on Lake Arenal — one of the largest lakes in Central America with dramatic volcano backdrop. Rent equipment from a local outfitter near the lake for approximately $25–35 per person.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the town of La Fortuna on foot. Browse local artisan shops for handmade crafts and souvenirs. Enjoy a casual dinner in town and try a traditional Tico dessert like tres leches cake or arroz con leche.

meals.breakfast: Lodge breakfast — eggs, gallo pinto, fresh juice, and coffee
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch provided by the hanging bridges tour operator, or eat at their on-site café — sandwiches and fresh fruit for ~$10–12
meals.dinner: Restaurante Don Rufino in La Fortuna — popular mid-range spot with excellent local and international dishes for ~$18–25

day_by_day.notes: Wear sturdy closed-toe shoes and long pants for the hanging bridges hike. Bring binoculars for wildlife spotting — this is one of the best bird-watching spots in Costa Rica. The lake can have strong winds in the afternoon, so check conditions before paddleboarding.

day_by_day.morning: White-water rafting on the Sarapiquí or Balsa River — a thrilling Class II–III rapids experience perfect for mid-level adventurers. Local operators like Desafío Adventure Company offer 2–3 hour guided rafting trips with all equipment included (~$65–85 per person). Spot birds and wildlife along the river banks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit La Fortuna Waterfall (Catarata La Fortuna) — a breathtaking 75-meter waterfall hidden in the jungle. Hike down 500+ steps to the base for a refreshing swim in the natural pool. The hike back up is a workout but absolutely worth it.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the lodge for a relaxing evening. Enjoy a second visit to the hot springs or simply unwind with a cold drink on the lodge terrace watching the volcano at sunset — if clouds permit, Arenal at dusk is spectacular.

meals.breakfast: Lodge breakfast — full Tico breakfast with gallo pinto, eggs, plantains, and coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at a soda near the waterfall entrance — casado or arroz con pollo for ~$8–10
meals.dinner: Lodge restaurant dinner — grilled chicken or fish with local vegetables and rice for ~$15–20

day_by_day.notes: Book rafting tours in advance, especially on weekends. The La Fortuna Waterfall charges an entrance fee of approximately $18 per person. Bring a waterproof camera or phone case for both activities. Wear swimwear under your clothes for the waterfall swim.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Arenal and travel to Monteverde Cloud Forest — approximately 3 to 4 hours via the scenic lake crossing (Jeep-Boat-Jeep route) which is far more adventurous than driving around. The boat crosses Lake Arenal and a 4WD jeep takes you up the winding mountain roads to Monteverde.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Monteverde and check into a mid-range lodge such as Monteverde Lodge or Arco Iris Ecolodge. Take an afternoon orientation walk through the Santa Elena Cloud Forest Reserve — a slightly less crowded alternative to the main Monteverde Reserve — to acclimatize to the altitude and misty cloud forest environment.
day_by_day.evening: Visit a local coffee or chocolate tour in the Monteverde area. Don Juan Coffee Tour or Café Monteverde offers evening tastings with explanations of the bean-to-cup process. Paired with artisan chocolate tasting, this is a perfect low-key evening activity.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the Arenal lodge before departure
meals.lunch: Pack snacks for the Jeep-Boat-Jeep journey or stop at a roadside café en route
meals.dinner: Dinner at Restaurante Morpho's in Santa Elena village — popular local spot with great casados and vegetarian options for ~$12–18

day_by_day.notes: The Jeep-Boat-Jeep transfer is iconic and highly recommended over the long road route — book in advance (~$35–45 per person). Monteverde roads are notoriously rough and unpaved; the boat route saves time and adds adventure. Pack a light jacket as cloud forest temperatures are cooler than the coast.

day_by_day.morning: Monteverde Cloud Forest Zip-Line Canopy Tour: Experience one of Costa Rica's most thrilling zip-line circuits soaring through the misty cloud forest canopy. Operators like Sky Adventures or Extremo Monteverde offer multi-cable circuits with platforms high above the forest floor, including a Tarzan swing and rappelling options. The views through the clouds are absolutely magical.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Monteverde Cloud Forest Biological Reserve — the crown jewel of Costa Rica's cloud forest system. Join a guided afternoon walk to spot the resplendent quetzal (February is an excellent time as it's nesting season), three-wattled bellbirds, emerald toucanets, and hundreds of orchid species.
day_by_day.evening: Night walk in the cloud forest with a naturalist guide — a completely different world emerges after dark. Spot sleeping birds, red-eyed tree frogs, stick insects, tarantulas, and glowing fungi with your guide's UV torch. A truly unforgettable experience.

meals.breakfast: Lodge breakfast — eggs, gallo pinto, fresh cloud forest honey, and locally grown coffee
meals.lunch: Café at the zip-line operator's base or packed lunch from the lodge — sandwiches and tropical fruit for ~$10
meals.dinner: Tree House Restaurant in Santa Elena — atmospheric dining in a multi-level restaurant built around a fig tree, with excellent local and international dishes for ~$18–25

day_by_day.notes: Book the zip-line tour and cloud forest reserve entry in advance — both have daily capacity limits. Wear closed-toe shoes and long sleeves for the zip-line. The night walk is typically 2 hours and costs ~$25–35 per person. February is one of the best months to spot the resplendent quetzal.

day_by_day.morning: Hummingbird Gallery visit near the Monteverde Reserve entrance — dozens of hummingbird species feed at feeders just inches from your face. Then explore the Orchid Garden in Santa Elena, home to over 450 orchid species including the world's smallest orchid (visible only with a magnifying glass).
day_by_day.afternoon: Depart Monteverde and travel to Tortuguero on the Caribbean coast — this is a long travel day requiring a combination of shuttle, bus, and boat. Arrange through a tour operator for the most seamless experience. The final leg by boat through jungle canals is a preview of what's to come.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive in Tortuguero village — a car-free, wildlife-rich community accessible only by boat or small plane. Check into a mid-range jungle lodge such as Manatus Hotel or Laguna Lodge. Enjoy a quiet evening listening to the sounds of the jungle.

meals.breakfast: Lodge breakfast in Monteverde before early departure
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or stop at a roadside restaurant en route — allow extra time for this
meals.dinner: Dinner at the Tortuguero lodge restaurant — fresh Caribbean-style rice and beans (different from Pacific coast style, cooked with coconut milk), jerk chicken or fish for ~$15–20

day_by_day.notes: This is the longest travel day of the trip — budget 8–10 hours total depending on connections. Book the Tortuguero transfer as a package through a reputable operator. Tortuguero is one of the most remote and rewarding destinations in Costa Rica — the journey is part of the experience.

day_by_day.morning: Tortuguero National Park Wildlife Boat Safari: Glide through the jungle waterways of Tortuguero on a guided boat safari. Your naturalist guide will navigate narrow canals lined with dense jungle, spotting caimans sunning on logs, river otters playing in the water, Jesus Christ lizards running on the surface, three-toed sloths hanging in cecropia trees, great green macaws, and an astonishing variety of herons and kingfishers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Tortuguero village on foot — a tiny, colorful Caribbean community with a fascinating mix of Afro-Caribbean and indigenous culture. Visit the Sea Turtle Conservancy Visitor Center to learn about Tortuguero's legendary sea turtle nesting program (green turtles nest here July–October, but leatherbacks nest February–July). Walk the jungle trail through the park independently.
day_by_day.evening: Evening canal walk along the village waterfront. If timing aligns with leatherback turtle season (February–July), arrange a guided nighttime beach walk to witness nesting sea turtles — one of the most profound wildlife experiences on Earth. Cost: ~$20–25 with a certified guide.

meals.breakfast: Lodge breakfast — Caribbean-style gallo pinto with coconut milk, fresh fruit, and strong coffee
meals.lunch: Miss Junies or Budda Café in Tortuguero village — local Caribbean rice and beans, fried plantains, and fresh juice for ~$10–12
meals.dinner: Lodge restaurant — whole fried snook or Caribbean-spiced chicken with coconut rice and beans for ~$15–20

day_by_day.notes: Tortuguero receives significant rainfall year-round — pack a quality rain jacket and waterproof bags for electronics. Mosquito repellent is essential. The boat safari is best in early morning when wildlife is most active. Turtle watching (if available) must be done with a licensed guide — never approach turtles independently.

day_by_day.morning: Second boat safari at dawn — early morning is prime wildlife viewing time in Tortuguero. This time explore different canal routes with your guide, looking for manatees (occasionally spotted), poison dart frogs on the canal banks, and the elusive Jesus Christ lizard. Bring binoculars for exceptional bird watching.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depart Tortuguero by boat and shuttle, traveling to the Osa Peninsula — home to Corcovado National Park. This is another long travel day requiring boat, shuttle, and possibly a domestic flight or ferry. Arrange through a tour operator. Arrive at a mid-range eco-lodge near Puerto Jiménez or Drake Bay.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at your Osa Peninsula lodge and settle in. Enjoy a briefing from your lodge naturalist about tomorrow's Corcovado expedition. The Osa Peninsula has an otherworldly atmosphere — the sounds of howler monkeys and scarlet macaws flying overhead at dusk are unforgettable.

meals.breakfast: Early lodge breakfast before departure — full Caribbean breakfast
meals.lunch: Pack snacks for the journey or stop at a restaurant in San José or Palmar Norte if routing through there
meals.dinner: Lodge restaurant on the Osa Peninsula — fresh seafood caught by local fishermen, served with rice, beans, and salad for ~$18–22

day_by_day.notes: The Tortuguero to Osa Peninsula journey is significant — consider whether a short domestic flight (Nature Air or Sansa, ~$100–150) makes more sense than the ground/boat combination. Book well in advance. The Osa Peninsula is one of the most biodiverse places on Earth — the anticipation is worth it.

day_by_day.morning: Corcovado National Park Jungle Expedition: Set out at first light with a certified guide for a full-day expedition into Corcovado — described by National Geographic as 'the most biologically intense place on Earth.' Trek through primary rainforest searching for all four Costa Rican monkey species (howler, spider, squirrel, and white-faced capuchin), Baird's tapirs, white-lipped peccaries, and the elusive jaguar tracks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue deeper into Corcovado on established trails. Spot scarlet macaws in massive flocks, harpy eagles soaring overhead, and an incredible diversity of reptiles, amphibians, and insects. Swim in a pristine jungle river pool during a midday break — a surreal experience surrounded by primary rainforest.
day_by_day.evening: Corcovado National Park Night Walk: As part of the full-day expedition package, venture into the jungle after dark with your guide. The night shift in Corcovado is extraordinary — fer-de-lance snakes, red-eyed tree frogs, porcupines, kinkajous, and bioluminescent organisms light up the forest floor. Return to the lodge exhausted but exhilarated.

meals.breakfast: Very early lodge breakfast at 5:00–5:30 AM before dawn departure
meals.lunch: Packed lunch provided by the tour operator or lodge — eaten in the jungle during a rest break: sandwiches, fruit, and plenty of water
meals.dinner: Lodge dinner upon return — hearty local meal to replenish energy: rice, beans, grilled meat, and vegetables for ~$15–20

day_by_day.notes: Corcovado requires an advance permit and a certified guide — you cannot enter independently. Book the full-day expedition well in advance (~$150–200 per person including guide, entrance fees, and packed lunch). Wear long pants, long sleeves, and sturdy waterproof boots. Bring at least 2–3 liters of water, sunscreen, and strong insect repellent. This is the most physically demanding day of the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning on the Osa Peninsula — take a leisurely walk on the beach near your lodge to spot scarlet macaws (they are remarkably common here) and dolphins playing in the surf. Visit a local artisan or cooperative to pick up final souvenirs — handmade jewelry, carved wood, or locally produced cacao products.
day_by_day.afternoon: Begin the journey back toward San José for departure. Depending on your return flight timing, either take a domestic flight from Puerto Jiménez (fastest option) or arrange a shuttle-ferry-shuttle combination back to the capital. If time allows, stop in the charming town of Quepos or Manuel Antonio for a final seafood lunch.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive in San José. If your return flight is the following day, check into an airport hotel such as Wyndham San José Herradura or Hampton Inn San José. Celebrate the end of an incredible 13-day Costa Rica adventure with a final dinner at a quality San José restaurant — try Restaurante Nuestra Tierra for a classic Costa Rican farewell meal in a beautifully decorated traditional setting.

meals.breakfast: Final lodge breakfast on the Osa — enjoy the jungle atmosphere one last time with fresh tropical fruit and locally grown coffee
meals.lunch: Seafood lunch at a restaurant in Quepos or along the route — ceviche, whole fried fish, and patacones for ~$15–18
meals.dinner: Restaurante Nuestra Tierra in San José — traditional Costa Rican cuisine in a festive atmosphere for ~$18–25 per person

day_by_day.notes: Confirm your return flight details and allow ample travel time from the Osa Peninsula to San José — ground transport can take 6–8 hours; domestic flight takes 45 minutes. Book the domestic flight in advance if using it. Keep a change of clothes and toiletries in your carry-on in case checked luggage is delayed on domestic connections. ¡Pura Vida!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Costa Rica Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Monteverde Cloud Forest Zip-Line Canopy Tour
experiences.description: Soar through the misty cloud forest canopy on one of Costa Rica's most thrilling zip-line circuits. With over 13 cables and Tarzan swings, you'll glide above the treetops spotting howler monkeys, toucans, and exotic orchids while experienced guides share insights about the unique cloud forest ecosystem.

experiences.name: Tortuguero National Park Wildlife Boat Safari
experiences.description: Glide through the jungle waterways of Tortuguero on a guided boat safari, spotting caimans, river otters, three-toed sloths, poison dart frogs, and over 300 bird species. If visiting between July and October, witness the awe-inspiring nesting of endangered green sea turtles on the beach at night.

experiences.name: Arenal Volcano Hanging Bridges & Rainforest Hike
experiences.description: Walk among the rainforest canopy on a network of 16 hanging bridges suspended high above the jungle floor near the iconic Arenal Volcano. This self-guided eco-walk offers incredible views of the volcano and exceptional wildlife spotting opportunities including toucans, morpho butterflies, and howler monkeys.

experiences.name: Manuel Antonio National Park Guided Wildlife Tour
experiences.description: Explore Costa Rica's most biodiverse national park with a certified naturalist guide who uses a high-powered spotting scope to reveal camouflaged wildlife invisible to the untrained eye. Encounter all four monkey species, two-toed sloths, Jesus Christ lizards, and stunning Pacific coastal beaches within the same park.

experiences.name: Corcovado National Park Jungle Expedition & Night Walk
experiences.description: Venture deep into one of the world's most biologically intense rainforests on the Osa Peninsula. A full-day guided trek through Corcovado reveals tapirs, scarlet macaws, white-lipped peccaries, and jaguars in their natural habitat. Cap the adventure with a guided night walk to spot tarantulas, tree frogs, and nocturnal mammals.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Juan Santamaría International Airport at 22:30 on flight UA. A private luxury transfer will be waiting to escort you to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, unwind with a welcome cocktail prepared by the resort's concierge, and settle into your beachfront suite.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in-flight or airport dining
meals.lunch: N/A — in-flight or airport dining
meals.dinner: Light late-night welcome amenity provided by the resort upon arrival — charcuterie board, tropical fruits, and sparkling wine in your suite

day_by_day.notes: Arrival is at 22:30, so no daytime activities are scheduled. Confirm private transfer in advance with the resort concierge. Ensure all luggage is collected before exiting customs. Request an early check-in amenity or turndown service so the room is fully prepared upon arrival.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the resort's signature ocean-view restaurant. Take a gentle orientation walk along the beachfront property, meet your dedicated concierge, and review the full 13-day itinerary. Dip in the infinity pool or enjoy a sunrise yoga session on the beach deck if offered by the resort.
day_by_day.afternoon: Enjoy a private resort experience — book a 90-minute couples' or solo spa treatment at the resort's wellness center featuring locally sourced volcanic mud wraps or rainforest botanical massages. Spend remaining afternoon hours lounging on the private beach or snorkeling in the calm coastal waters.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at the resort's beachfront bar, followed by a premium tasting menu dinner at the resort's flagship fine-dining restaurant. Ask the sommelier to pair Costa Rican craft beers or South American wines with each course.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet breakfast at the resort's ocean-view restaurant — fresh tropical fruits, eggs Benedict, Costa Rican gallo pinto, freshly brewed local coffee
meals.lunch: Light poolside lunch — ceviche, grilled fish tacos, and fresh coconut water at the resort's beach club
meals.dinner: Multi-course tasting menu at the resort's signature fine-dining restaurant — local seafood, prime cuts, and tropical desserts paired with curated wines

day_by_day.notes: This is a dedicated recovery and orientation day after the late arrival. No off-site excursions are scheduled. Use this day to acclimate to the time zone, humidity, and tropical climate. Confirm all upcoming excursion bookings with your concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Private luxury transfer departs early morning toward Manuel Antonio National Park (approximately 2.5–3 hours from most beachfront resort locations). Upon arrival, begin the Manuel Antonio National Park Guided Wildlife Tour with a certified naturalist guide equipped with high-powered spotting scopes. Spot white-faced capuchin monkeys, two-toed sloths, scarlet macaws, and Jesus Christ lizards in one of Costa Rica's most biodiverse ecosystems.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the morning wildlife tour, enjoy a picnic-style gourmet lunch prepared by the resort or a premium local restaurant near the park entrance. Spend the early afternoon relaxing on Playa Manuel Antonio — one of the most beautiful beaches in Central America — before a leisurely return transfer to the resort.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at a highly regarded farm-to-table restaurant near the resort. Enjoy locally sourced ingredients, fresh-caught Pacific seafood, and handcrafted tropical cocktails in an open-air jungle setting.

meals.breakfast: Early gourmet breakfast at the resort before departure — açaí bowls, fresh pastries, and Costa Rican coffee
meals.lunch: Premium packed gourmet picnic or lunch at a top-rated local restaurant near Manuel Antonio — grilled snapper, plantains, and fresh tropical juices
meals.dinner: Farm-to-table fine dining near the resort — ceviche, hearts of palm salad, grilled mahi-mahi, and artisanal desserts

day_by_day.notes: Wear lightweight, breathable clothing and sturdy closed-toe shoes for the wildlife tour. Apply reef-safe sunscreen and bring insect repellent. The naturalist guide will use a high-powered scope to spot wildlife in the treetops. Book this tour well in advance as Manuel Antonio is extremely popular.

day_by_day.morning: Private luxury transfer departs for Arenal Volcano region (approximately 3.5–4 hours). Check in to a premium eco-lodge or luxury boutique hotel near Arenal for a two-night stay. After settling in, embark on the Arenal Volcano Hanging Bridges & Rainforest Hike — walk among the rainforest canopy on a network of 16 hanging bridges suspended high above the jungle floor, spotting toucans, howler monkeys, and exotic flora.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the hanging bridges experience, visit the world-renowned Tabacón Grand Spa Thermal Resort. Soak in natural hot spring pools fed by the Arenal Volcano's geothermal energy, surrounded by lush rainforest. Opt for a private spa treatment such as a volcanic stone massage or hydrotherapy session.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Restaurante Arenal 1968 or a comparable premium restaurant with direct volcano views. Watch the sunset illuminate the slopes of Arenal Volcano while enjoying Costa Rican cuisine elevated with fine-dining techniques.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before departure — tropical fruit platters, eggs to order, and local coffee
meals.lunch: Gourmet lunch at the eco-lodge or a premium restaurant near the hanging bridges — grilled chicken, rice and beans, fresh salads
meals.dinner: Premium volcano-view dinner — filet mignon, fresh river trout, yuca fries, and locally sourced desserts with artisanal chocolate

day_by_day.notes: The Arenal region can experience afternoon rain showers — pack a light rain jacket. The hanging bridges hike is moderate in difficulty; wear sturdy hiking shoes. Book the Tabacón hot springs in advance as private access and spa treatments fill up quickly. Confirm the two-night Arenal accommodation with your concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Full day in the Arenal region. Begin with an early guided birdwatching walk around the eco-lodge grounds or along the Arenal Lake shoreline, spotting toucans, hummingbirds, and herons with a private naturalist guide. Enjoy the crisp morning air and dramatic volcano backdrop.
day_by_day.afternoon: Optional adventure activity: white-water rafting on the Balsa or Sarapiquí River (Class II–IV rapids depending on preference), or a private kayaking excursion on Lake Arenal with stunning volcano views. Both options can be arranged through a premium adventure outfitter with top-tier safety equipment.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the eco-lodge for a private sunset cocktail experience on your terrace or balcony overlooking Arenal Volcano. Enjoy a curated in-room dining experience or dine at the lodge's signature restaurant with a specially crafted menu featuring locally foraged ingredients and premium Costa Rican rum cocktails.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet breakfast at the eco-lodge — banana pancakes, tropical smoothies, gallo pinto, and local cheese platters
meals.lunch: Riverside or lakeside picnic lunch arranged by the outfitter — sandwiches, fresh fruit, energy bars, and cold beverages
meals.dinner: Private terrace dinner or lodge restaurant — slow-braised short rib, hearts of palm ceviche, and passion fruit panna cotta

day_by_day.notes: Day 5 is a flexible day in Arenal — use it to recharge or add adventure based on energy levels. The Balsa River rafting is suitable for most fitness levels; confirm difficulty level with the outfitter. Lake Arenal kayaking is a serene, low-intensity alternative perfect for wildlife spotting.

day_by_day.morning: Private luxury transfer from Arenal to Monteverde Cloud Forest region (approximately 2.5–3 hours via scenic mountain roads). Check in to a premium cloud forest lodge. After settling in, take a leisurely orientation walk through the lodge's private nature reserve, spotting the iconic resplendent quetzal if the season is favorable.
day_by_day.afternoon: Embark on the Monteverde Cloud Forest Zip-Line Canopy Tour — soar through the misty cloud forest canopy on one of Costa Rica's most thrilling zip-line circuits. Experience multiple lines, Tarzan swings, and rappelling sections with panoramic views of the cloud forest. A premium operator will provide top-of-the-line harness systems and expert guides.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a premium night walk through the Monteverde Cloud Forest Reserve with a private naturalist guide. Spot kinkajous, glass frogs, tarantulas, and sleeping birds using specialized UV and infrared flashlights. Return to the lodge for a warming dinner featuring cloud forest–inspired cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the Arenal eco-lodge before departure — fresh fruit, eggs, toast, and coffee
meals.lunch: Gourmet lunch at the Monteverde lodge upon arrival — black bean soup, grilled chicken, and fresh tropical juices
meals.dinner: Lodge restaurant dinner after the night walk — creamy mushroom risotto with local fungi, pan-seared fish, and artisanal Costa Rican chocolate dessert

day_by_day.notes: Monteverde is significantly cooler than coastal areas — pack a light fleece or jacket for evenings and the night walk. The zip-line canopy tour has weight and health restrictions; confirm eligibility in advance. The night walk requires closed-toe shoes and long pants to protect against insects.

day_by_day.morning: Full day in Monteverde. Begin with an early guided birdwatching tour inside the Monteverde Cloud Forest Biological Reserve — one of the most biodiverse cloud forests in the world. A private ornithologist guide will help locate the resplendent quetzal, three-wattled bellbird, and over 400 other bird species found in the reserve.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Don Juan Coffee, Chocolate & Sugar Cane Tour for a premium behind-the-scenes experience of Costa Rica's most celebrated agricultural exports. Taste single-origin coffees, handmade chocolates, and fresh sugarcane juice in an intimate, expert-led setting. Alternatively, explore the Selvatura Park's hummingbird garden and butterfly observatory.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in Monteverde at a premium restaurant such as Celajes Restaurant at the El Establo Mountain Hotel, offering sweeping views of the Gulf of Nicoya. Enjoy a curated menu of Costa Rican fusion cuisine with fine wines.

meals.breakfast: Early gourmet breakfast at the cloud forest lodge — granola, tropical fruits, eggs, and Monteverde-grown coffee
meals.lunch: Premium tasting lunch at the coffee and chocolate tour — artisanal cheeses, fresh bread, single-origin chocolate, and specialty coffees
meals.dinner: Fine-dining dinner with panoramic views — grilled tenderloin, lobster bisque, and a decadent chocolate lava cake made with locally sourced cacao

day_by_day.notes: The Monteverde Cloud Forest Biological Reserve requires advance ticket booking — secure entry through your concierge. Early morning (6:00–8:00 AM) offers the best wildlife sightings before other visitors arrive. Bring binoculars and a camera with a zoom lens for birdwatching.

day_by_day.morning: Private luxury transfer from Monteverde to Tortuguero National Park (approximately 4–5 hours, including a scenic boat ride through jungle canals). The journey itself is part of the experience — enjoy the transition from cloud forest to lowland Caribbean jungle. Check in to a premium eco-lodge inside or adjacent to the park.
day_by_day.afternoon: After settling in, embark on the Tortuguero National Park Wildlife Boat Safari — glide through the jungle waterways on a guided boat safari, spotting caimans, river otters, green sea turtles, manatees, and an extraordinary variety of waterbirds including roseate spoonbills and anhingas. Your expert guide will navigate the labyrinthine canal system with precision.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the eco-lodge for a sunset cocktail on the river-view deck. Enjoy dinner at the lodge's premium restaurant featuring Caribbean-inspired cuisine with fresh local ingredients. If the season permits (February can be off-season for nesting), inquire about a guided sea turtle observation experience on the beach.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the Monteverde lodge before departure — eggs, fresh fruit, and local coffee
meals.lunch: Gourmet packed lunch enjoyed on the boat transfer to Tortuguero — sandwiches, fresh fruit, and cold beverages
meals.dinner: Caribbean-fusion dinner at the eco-lodge — coconut curry shrimp, jerk chicken, rice and beans cooked in coconut milk, and tropical fruit sorbet

day_by_day.notes: Tortuguero is accessible only by boat or small aircraft — the journey is part of the adventure. Pack light for the boat transfer. Bring waterproof bags for cameras and electronics. The wildlife boat safari is best in early morning or late afternoon; the afternoon session on arrival is ideal. Confirm sea turtle observation availability with the lodge.

day_by_day.morning: Rise before dawn for a premium early-morning wildlife boat safari through Tortuguero's secondary canals — the best time to spot elusive wildlife including river otters, Jesus Christ lizards, poison dart frogs, and dozens of waterbird species. A private naturalist guide will maximize sightings with expert knowledge of the canal system.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Tortuguero Village on foot — a charming, car-free Caribbean community accessible only by boat. Visit the Sea Turtle Conservancy Visitor Center to learn about Tortuguero's world-famous leatherback and green sea turtle conservation programs. Browse local artisan shops and enjoy a leisurely afternoon at the lodge's pool or riverside deck.
day_by_day.evening: Premium private dinner experience at the eco-lodge — request a special riverside or candlelit beach dinner if available. Enjoy a curated menu with Caribbean seafood, tropical cocktails, and a stargazing session guided by the lodge's naturalist staff.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast before the dawn boat safari — granola bars, fruit, and coffee provided by the lodge
meals.lunch: Late-morning brunch back at the lodge after the safari — full hot breakfast spread with Caribbean flavors, fresh juices, and local pastries
meals.dinner: Private premium dinner experience — whole grilled snapper, lobster tail, plantain chips, and a decadent tres leches cake

day_by_day.notes: Dawn wildlife safaris (departing at 5:30–6:00 AM) offer dramatically better wildlife sightings than afternoon tours. Bring a light rain jacket as Tortuguero receives significant rainfall year-round. Insect repellent is essential — long sleeves and pants are recommended for evening activities.

day_by_day.morning: Private luxury transfer from Tortuguero back to the Pacific side of Costa Rica, heading toward the Osa Peninsula and Corcovado National Park (approximately 6–7 hours including boat and road transfers, or opt for a premium domestic charter flight for approximately 1 hour). Check in to a premium eco-lodge on the Osa Peninsula.
day_by_day.afternoon: After arriving and settling in, enjoy a brief orientation hike on the eco-lodge's private trails. The Osa Peninsula is one of the most biologically intense regions on Earth — even a short walk can yield sightings of scarlet macaws, white-lipped peccaries, and poison dart frogs. Relax by the lodge's pool or on the private beach.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at the eco-lodge's premium open-air restaurant, featuring locally sourced Osa Peninsula ingredients — fresh Pacific seafood, tropical fruits, and organic vegetables from the lodge's garden. Enjoy cocktails made with local tropical fruits and premium spirits.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at Tortuguero lodge before departure — eggs, gallo pinto, tropical fruits, and coffee
meals.lunch: Gourmet packed lunch or stop at a premium restaurant en route — fresh ceviche, grilled fish, and cold beverages
meals.dinner: Open-air eco-lodge dinner — grilled Pacific snapper, pineapple salsa, yuca fries, and passion fruit cheesecake

day_by_day.notes: The transfer to the Osa Peninsula is lengthy by road and boat. A domestic charter flight (approximately $200–$400 per person) is strongly recommended for a premium experience and to maximize time on the Osa Peninsula. Book the charter flight well in advance through your concierge. Confirm Corcovado National Park permits for the following day — entry is strictly limited and requires advance booking.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day Corcovado National Park Jungle Expedition — depart early with a private certified guide for the Corcovado National Park Jungle Expedition & Night Walk. Venture deep into one of the world's most biologically intense rainforests, home to Baird's tapirs, jaguar tracks, four species of monkeys, harpy eagles, and an extraordinary density of wildlife. The morning section covers primary rainforest trails with expert naturalist commentary.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Corcovado expedition through the afternoon — explore river crossings, remote beach sections, and dense primary jungle. Enjoy a gourmet packed lunch in the heart of the national park. Your guide will maximize wildlife encounters using expert tracking skills and knowledge of animal behavior patterns.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the eco-lodge and freshen up before the optional Night Walk component of the Corcovado experience — spot nocturnal species including fer-de-lance snakes, giant huntsman spiders, red-eyed tree frogs, and tapirs using specialized lighting equipment. Return for a well-earned premium dinner at the lodge.

meals.breakfast: Early gourmet breakfast at the eco-lodge before departure — protein-rich eggs, fresh fruit, and strong local coffee
meals.lunch: Premium gourmet packed lunch in Corcovado National Park — artisan sandwiches, energy bars, tropical fruits, and filtered water
meals.dinner: Celebratory premium dinner at the eco-lodge after the expedition — surf and turf, fresh ceviche, tropical dessert, and a glass of fine wine or premium rum

day_by_day.notes: The Corcovado expedition is physically demanding — wear sturdy waterproof hiking boots and long pants. River crossings may be required depending on the trail. The park's strict entry limits mean private guided access is essential. Carry only what is necessary — a small daypack with water, sunscreen, and insect repellent. This is one of the most extraordinary wildlife experiences in the world.

day_by_day.morning: A well-deserved rest morning after the Corcovado expedition. Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the eco-lodge. Optional gentle morning activity: a private yoga or stretching session on the beach, or a guided dolphin and whale watching boat tour off the Osa Peninsula coast (humpback whales and spinner dolphins are commonly spotted in this area).
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury transfer or charter flight back to the main resort — Aegean Bliss Resort. Arrive in the afternoon and enjoy a welcome-back experience at the resort: refresh in your beachfront suite, take a sunset swim in the ocean, and visit the spa for a restorative treatment to ease any muscle soreness from the Corcovado expedition.
day_by_day.evening: Premium sunset dinner on the beach — arrange a private candlelit table on the sand through the resort concierge. Enjoy a curated seafood menu with champagne, fresh lobster, and a dessert platter as you watch the Pacific sunset on your penultimate evening.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely full gourmet breakfast at the Osa eco-lodge — tropical smoothie bowls, eggs Benedict, local pastries, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the eco-lodge or en route — fresh fruit, sandwiches, and cold beverages
meals.dinner: Private beachfront candlelit dinner at Aegean Bliss Resort — champagne, lobster thermidor, grilled vegetables, and a decadent chocolate fondant with tropical fruit coulis

day_by_day.notes: Confirm the private beachfront dinner setup with the resort concierge at least 48 hours in advance. The dolphin and whale watching tour departs early from Drake Bay or Puerto Jiménez — confirm timing with the Osa eco-lodge. Pack all belongings the night before departure from the Osa to ensure a smooth morning transfer.
